## Overview

Fixes the shared-prefix junction under per-group EAGLE flags (#61455): with a dropping EAGLE group in the lookup, siblings that share a prefix get 0 prefix-cache hits under sparse retention (default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`). The junction becomes a set of positions, `{J - A, J}`, computed in one place (`junction_boundaries()`) and used by every junction consumer. This is an alternative to #62206, which keeps an extra SWA tail at `J - block_size` inside the SWA mask only.

The MooncakeStore side (store lookup as a junction source, `store_mask` as a consumer) is a follow-up PR stacked on this one: #62400.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP (retention 0): siblings that diverge 8 tokens past an aligned shared prefix of 3840 tokens get 0 hit tokens on main and 3584 with this PR. Siblings that diverge 160 tokens past it get 3840 on both.
- Shared-prefix GSM8K (1319 questions): the prefix-cache hit rate goes from 4.7% to 82.1%, and accuracy does not change (0.943 → 0.945).
- One helper produces the junction; all consumers read it: SWA and Mamba retention masks, the Mamba junction checkpoint, the scheduler's chunk stops (one per position) and `OffloadingConnector`.
- No behavior change without EAGLE, or when no dropping (non-Mamba) EAGLE group takes part in the lookup.

## Validation

**End to end** (GB200, 4 GPUs, base 83c9a547bf):

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

Junction probe: requests A, B, C, D share exactly F + d token ids (F = 3840 = 15 × 256), then each has its own 1500-token suffix. They are sent one at a time; the table shows `cached_tokens` of C and D.

| d | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0, 0 | 3584, 3584 |
| 160 | 3840, 3840 | 3840, 3840 |

Shared-prefix GSM8K: every prompt is the same 3848-token prefix (instructions, 8 train exemplars, filler), then about 600 tokens of per-question distractor text, then the test question. 1319 questions, concurrency 32, greedy, `max_tokens` 512.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| accuracy | 0.943 | 0.945 |
| prefix-cache hit rate (`vllm:prefix_cache_hits / queries`) | 4.7% | 82.1% |
| `cached_tokens` per question | 0 for 1248 questions | 3584 for 1247, 3840 for 71 |

The per-question suffix is longer than the hit alignment on purpose. With a shorter suffix, a request's own prompt-end replay tail lands on the shared prefix and hides the bug.

**Unit tests** (CPU):

```
pytest -n 16 tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_*.py \
  --deselect tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate \
  --deselect tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py
1695 passed
```

`test_swa_shared_prefix_reuse_under_zero_retention_eagle` covers uniform and mixed block sizes, with only the SWA draft group flagged and with all groups flagged. `test_mamba_shared_prefix_reuse_eagle_draft_group` covers a Mamba hybrid with a flagged draft group. The offloading scheduler test checks that every junction position is a reachable boundary. The flagged cases fail on main.

## Details

**Root cause.** The junction is where the longest single-group hit exceeds the reconciled hit. A dropping EAGLE group needs a peek block past its hit. So after #61455, a sibling that shares F tokens hits F in a non-EAGLE group but at most F − A in the dropping group (A = hit alignment). Main pinned only F, and no sibling can resume there.

**Why a set.** Where a sibling resumes depends on how far past F it diverges. Divergence of less than the drop unit past F resumes at F − A; divergence further than that resumes at F. When the drop unit is smaller than A (DeepSeek-V4: SWA block 64, A 256), both cases occur, so a single position cannot serve both. The junction is therefore `{F − A, F}` whenever a dropping EAGLE group takes part in the lookup.

**Why not #62206.** #62206 fixes the SWA mask only. The Mamba checkpoint, the scheduler chunk stop and `OffloadingConnector` keep the wrong junction.

**Supersedes the first version of this PR.** The first version moved the junction to `F − A` only. That lost the hit at F for siblings that diverge further than the drop unit (a regression with mixed block sizes). This version keeps both positions.

**Cost.** One extra retained tail per junction, only when a dropping EAGLE group exists. Without EAGLE, the junction is one position, as on main.

---

+            enable_caching=True,
+            hash_block_size=hash_block_size,
+            retention_interval=0,
+            use_eagle=True,
+        )
+        shared = 64  # F: 4 hash blocks shared with every later request
+        cover = shared + max(32, *sibling_deltas)
+
+        def allocate_chunked(req, nc, cb, ends):

+        manager.coordinator.new_step_starts()
+        owner = make_request("owner", [7] * cover + [900] * 64, hash_block_size, sha256)
+        cb, nc, junctions = manager.get_computed_blocks(owner)
+        assert junctions == ()
+        allocate_chunked(owner, nc, cb, [len(owner.all_token_ids)])
+
+        # The detector shares `shared` tokens: full16 hits F, the dropping
+        # draft group lands back on the 32-grid, Mamba lags at 0.
+        manager.coordinator.new_step_starts()
+        det = make_request("det", [7] * shared + [800] * 32, hash_block_size, sha256)
+        cb, nc, junctions = manager.get_computed_blocks(det)
+        assert nc == 0
+        # Both resume positions are kept: F - A and F.
+        assert junctions == (shared - alignment, shared)
+        det.shared_prefix_boundaries = junctions

+        allocate_chunked(det, nc, cb, [*junctions, len(det.all_token_ids)])
+
+        hits = []
+        for d in sibling_deltas:

+def junction_boundaries(
+    longest_hit: int, hit: int, alignment: int, expand_eagle: bool

+    """Positions a sibling sharing a prefix up to ``longest_hit`` can resume at.

+    one; a junction exists only where they diverge. With a dropping EAGLE

+    past ``longest_hit`` cannot verify its peek block and resumes one

+    ``longest_hit``, so both positions are kept.
